---
title: "Announcements"
---

Use an announcement for a short message that applies to the whole documentation
site, such as a development-version warning or a temporary service notice.
Configure Quarto's native `website.announcement`; Askr supplies the layout,
colors and accessible controls.

The bar at the top of this Gallery is a demonstration notice. It does not
describe a pending Askr release.

## Configure a notice

```yaml
website:
  announcement:
    content: "Development documentation — this version has not been released."
    icon: info-circle
    type: warning
    dismissable: false
    position: above-navbar
```

Choose `warning` for a development-version notice. Keep `dismissable: false`
when the message must remain visible throughout reading. For a temporary
notice readers may acknowledge, use `dismissable: true`; its close button works
with the keyboard. Quarto remembers dismissal in that browser for the current
announcement.

The text can contain Markdown links and wraps on narrow screens. `icon` is an
optional [Bootstrap icon name](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/); omit it for a
text-only notice. `position: below-navbar` places the same bar beneath the
navigation. Askr keeps the Pages control in the navigation row in either
position, including when the announcement wraps onto several lines.

## Languages and version context

Put the translated message in each language site's `_quarto.yml`. For example,
the Traditional Chinese site can use:

```yaml
website:
  announcement:
    content: "開發版文件：此版本尚未正式發佈。"
    icon: info-circle
    type: warning
    dismissable: false
    position: above-navbar
```

Use the same intent in each translation. The author or documentation build
chooses the message for each published version; Askr does not infer package
release status from the version selector. Remove `website.announcement` when
there is no site-wide notice.

## Appearance and behavior

Askr uses a quiet tinted surface, a semantic accent and visible link and focus
styles in both themes. The notice follows the site's light/dark selection.
The icon, text and optional close control occupy separate
spaces; long text can wrap without covering navigation controls. The native
header continues to account for the bar when positioning the article, sidebars
and page anchors.

Use this configuration without adding consumer CSS or JavaScript. The available
`type`, `icon`, `position` and `dismissable` settings remain Quarto's native
options; see the [Quarto announcement guide](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-tools.html#announcement-bar).
